title: Remap a shortcut is not working when targeting git-bash
author: juanjetomas
summary: App-specific remaps targeting git-bash.exe do not apply because the focused terminal window belongs to mintty.exe, while global rules and rules targeting mintty.exe work.

confidence.rationale: The process mismatch is confirmed, but safe descendant identity and user-facing semantics require product/code review.

judgment.rationale: A current 0.100.2 reproduction identifies the exact process boundary. The remaining product decision is how launcher/child-process targeting should be represented safely.
evidence: Shift+A to B targeted to git-bash.exe leaves A unchanged.
The same mapping works globally and in Chrome.
A current reproducer confirmed that targeting mintty.exe works because mintty owns the foreground window and is a child of git-bash.exe.
judgment.recommended_action: Design explicit launcher/descendant process targeting or improve the editor's process selection guidance without broad accidental matches.

fix_assessment.rationale: No active merged fix covers the scoped PowerToys-owned path. The bug is not generic shortcut dispatch. A safe fix must define whether app targeting means current foreground executable, launcher's process tree, or an explicit group, then make that choice visible in the editor.

proposed_fixes.title: Make launcher-child targeting explicit for app-specific remaps
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Keyboard Manager compares the configured application name with the foreground window's executable; Git Bash's visible window belongs to mintty.exe rather than the git-bash.exe launcher.
plan: Document and expose the actual foreground executable when selecting a target application.
Evaluate an explicit optional descendant/process-group target rather than silently matching every child of a launcher.
Add process-target tests for direct executables, launchers with terminal children, unrelated descendants, and process restarts.
verification: Target mintty.exe and confirm the remap applies only in Git Bash terminals.
If descendant targeting is added, target git-bash.exe and verify only its intended terminal child matches while unrelated mintty instances do not.

confidence.rationale: The process mismatch is confirmed, but safe descendant identity and user-facing semantics require product/code review.

issue_context.summary: App-specific remaps targeting git-bash.exe do not apply because the focused terminal window belongs to mintty.exe, while global rules and rules targeting mintty.exe work.
known_information: The issue was reproduced on PowerToys 0.100.2 with Git 2.53.0.2.
The runtime matcher uses the focused process identity, which is mintty.exe for Git Bash.
A closed older issue reported similar Git targeting behavior.
inferences: Matching every descendant automatically could be surprising or unsafe for general launchers; the editor may need an explicit option or resolved foreground-process selection.
issue_context.analysis: The bug is not generic shortcut dispatch. A safe fix must define whether app targeting means current foreground executable, launcher's process tree, or an explicit group, then make that choice visible in the editor.
initial_investigation: Read the body, all comments, labels, and related closed issue.
Used the current git-bash.exe versus mintty.exe reproduction to localize process matching.

reproduce.title: Compare git-bash.exe and mintty.exe app targets
reproduce.version_requirement: Current stable PowerToys release unless the issue names a required preview build
prerequisites: Git for Windows with Git Bash
A harmless Shift+A to B test remap
setup: Create an app-specific remap targeting git-bash.exe.
Open Git Bash and a separate ordinary application.
steps: Press Shift+A in Git Bash and record the foreground executable.
Change only the target to mintty.exe and repeat.
Confirm the rule does not apply in the ordinary application.
reproduce.expected_result: The editor/runtime should clearly target the process that owns the window, or an explicit safe launcher-child scope should work predictably.
